==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|bĭz'i}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪz.i/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-busy.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-busy.ogg|a=UK}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-busy.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{hyphenation|en|bus|y}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪzi|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|bisy}}, {{m|enm|busie}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bisiġ|t=busy, occupied, diligent}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bisīg|t=diligent; zealous; busy}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|biesich|t=active, diligent, hard-working, industrious}}, {{cog|nl|bezig|t=busy}}, {{cog|nds|besig|t=busy}}. The spelling with ⟨u⟩ represents the pronunciation of the West Midland and Southern dialects while the Modern English pronunciation with {{IPAchar|/ɪ/}} is from the dialects of the East Midlands.Upward, Christopher & George Davidson. 2011. [https://books.google.com/books?id=fNfebt79zdwC&pg=PT85 ''The History of English Spelling'']. Wiley-Blackwell. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|busie||obsolete}} ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er}} # Crowded with business or activities; having a [[great deal]] [[going on]]. #: {{syn|en|heavy|bustling}} #: {{ux|en|Be careful crossing that '''busy''' street.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|V|iii|passage=To-morrow is a '''busy''' day.}} #* {{RQ:Dickens Christmas Carol|text=Although they had but that moment left the school behind them, they were now in the '''busy''' thoroughfares of a city, where shadowy passengers passed and repassed; where shadowy carts and coaches battled for the way, and all the strife and tumult of a real city were.{{...}}They left the '''busy''' scene, and went into an obscure part of the town, where Scrooge had never penetrated before, although he recognised its situation, and its bad repute.}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Peter Eavis|title=Counteroffers Exchanged in Effort to Avert U.S. Dock Strike|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/30/business/port-strike-dockworkers.html|date=30-09-2024|passage=With hours to go before their labor contract expired, longshoremen on the East and Gulf Coasts prepared on Monday to go on strike at midnight, halting most activity at some of the '''busiest''' U.S. ports.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001022440/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/30/business/port-strike-dockworkers.html}} # {{U|engaged}} with or [[preoccupy|preoccupied]] by an [[activity]] or [[person]]. #: {{ux|en|The director cannot see you now: he's '''busy'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Her telephone has been '''busy''' all day.}} #: {{ux|en|He is '''busy''' with piano practice.}} #: {{ux|en|Ramzi is '''busy''' getting ready for meetings.}} #: {{ux|en|Go away, I’m '''busy''' sleeping!}} #* {{RQ:Defoe Robinson Crusoe|passage=And the first thing I did was to lay by a certain quantity of provisions, being the stores for our voyage; and intended in a week or a fortnight’s time to open the dock, and launch out our boat. I was '''busy''' one morning upon something of this kind, when I called to Friday, and bid him to go to the sea-shore and see if he could find a turtle or a tortoise, a thing which we generally got once a week, for the sake of the eggs as well as the flesh.
But to return to Friday; he was so '''busy''' about his father that I could not find in my heart to take him off for some time; but after I thought he could leave him a little, I called him to me, and he came jumping and laughing, and pleased to the highest extreme: then I asked him if he had given his father any bread.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|text=After walking several miles in a leisurely manner, and too '''busy''' to know anything about it, they found at last, on examining their watches, that it was time to be at home.}} #* {{RQ:Dickens Christmas Carol|text=His hands were '''busy''' with his garments all this time; turning them inside out, putting them on upside down, tearing them, mislaying them, making them parties to every kind of extravagance.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Hannah Seligson|title=Where to get hip in Palm Beach|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/palm-beach-best-spots-2017|date=2017-03-01|passage=It may get even '''busier''' in town when a sleek train service called the Brightline debuts this summer, shuttling travelers between nearby West Palm Beach and Miami.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812221354/https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/palm-beach-best-spots-2017}} # Having much [[work]] to do; having much to get done. #: {{nearsyn|en|swamped}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Jennifer Cohen|title=Always busy? 8 ways to stay fit|url=https://www.cnn.com/2015/06/19/health/fitness-strategy-busy-people|date=2015-06-19|passage=Finding the time to work out and cook healthy meals is easily pushed to the wayside in our ordinary, '''busy''' lives.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815202639/https://www.cnn.com/2015/06/19/health/fitness-strategy-busy-people}} # Having a lot going on; [[complicated]] or [[intricate]]. #: {{ux|en|Flowers, stripes, and checks in the same fabric make for a '''busy''' pattern.}} # {{U|officious}}; meddling. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|IV|ii|line=130|text=I will be hanged if some eternal villain,
Some '''busy''' and insinuating rogue,
Some cogging, cozening slave, to get some office,
Have not devised this slander; I'll be hanged else.}} =====Synonyms===== * {{l|en|swamped}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|busihead| keep someone busy| busy belt|business|busy I could hardly believe it when I spotted it poking out of the rubble. Excitedly, I ran straight home and gave it to my mum. I was hero of the hour until I got into trouble with the '''busies''' – the police – soon afterwards for pinching a bottle of milk from a float.}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|bisien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bisgian|t=to occupy, employ, trouble, afflict}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bisīgōn}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|bisgia|t=to use}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive|usually [[reflexive]]}} To make somebody busy or active; to [[occupy]]. #: {{usex|en|On my vacation I'll '''busy''' myself with gardening.}} #: {{usex|en|The work '''busied''' me all afternoon.}} #* {{quote-web|en|date=22 June 2026|author=Sam Woodhouse|work=BBC News|title={{w|Alan Greenspan}}, architect of the modern American economy, dies aged 100|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjer7x7yl12o|text=And while his fellow musicians spent their evenings smoking marijuana, Alan Greenspan '''busied himself''' by swotting up on economics and doing the band's accounts.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261004173708/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjer7x7yl12o|archivedate=4 October 2026}} =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|bebusy}} * {{l|en|busy around}} * {{l|en|forebusy}} * {{l|en|overbusy}} *{{l|en| rebusy}} * {{l|en|unbusy}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to keep busy with}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Portuguese: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to rush somebody}} * Finnish: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== * {{R:OneLook}} * {{R:Century}} {{reflist}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=bsuy|buys}} {{cln|en|terms with Middle English front rounded vowel spellings|terms with mixed convergence|}}
